And the agenda states that it's to deal with the adoption of a decision to declare the Autonomous Region of Krajina, the state of the deputies financing the work of the Krajina, and the radio and television subscription. The document bears no stamp. It's simply the typed version of Mr. Kupresanin's name in Cyrillic. The next document, P80, is the statute, which I believe we have already looked at. The document after that, P81, is the decision on the proclamation of the Autonomous Region of Krajina as an inseparable part of the Federal State of Federative Yugoslavia. And again, there is on this occasion a stamp and a signature apparently suggesting it's Vojo Kupresanin. P82, Your Honours, is a report -- or it's a letter enclosing a report on the activity of the -- of what's called armed groups on the territory of the security services centre. If Your Honours -- because there is a link in this sense only that it appears again. Your Honours need to go to P95, which should be behind divider 11.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's according to your numbering.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Oh, we're on P --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: P95 is in our case behind divider 42.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right. Oh, yes, because -- but it should -- it's an extract from the minutes from the tenth session of the Assembly of the Autonomous Region. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, item 2 there includes a report of the Banja Luka Security Services Centre on the criminal and illegal activities of Veljko Milankovic and other members of a paramilitary formation from Prnjavor, was submitted by Stojan Zupljanin. So although the report is dated the 20th of September -- and I think all we can do is suggest that this seems to be the report, because if one reads through the report, that is what it is about. And Milankovic was the gentleman referred to by the last witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I now must enter another objection, because Ms. Korner is making a connection between two documents that is not on its face a proper connection. She's arguing based upon the content that these two documents are connected. That's argument. It's improper at this stage. I therefore object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I've got nothing to say, Your Honour. The point of this exercise is not to comment or whatever but so that Your Honours can understand --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We don't want an argument. It's just a suggestion. She actually used the word "suggestion," so the objection is not sustained.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then, Your Honour, if we go back, please, to document P83, Your Honour, this is a document from the 2nd of October, 1991, from the assistant to the Minister of the Interior, addressed to the CSB, the SJB, and the SUP seeking a breakdown of numbering and percentages of the ethnic structure of reserve members of the police forces. Your Honour, the next document, P84 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Now, here we have a problem, Ms. Korner, because I at least have only the B/C/S text. I don't have the English translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: That's the same for everybody. Your Honour, we're making a note --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You have it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we made a note, and we're going to supply all the missing documents. Your Honour, it is in fact a document headed "The Assembly of the Autonomous Region of Bosanska Krajina -- Bosnian Krajina, Banja Luka." And it's signed and sealed by Mr. Kupresanin, and is apparently a request or demand that a member called Mr. Bogojevic [phoen] be replaced by Professor Koljevic, Dr. Koljevic. Your Honour, the next document, P85, is the minutes of the SDS -- the minutes of a party council held on the 15th of October, 1991. And it says it's the agenda. And it's also apparently part of the things that were said during that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The Defence contests this document because it hasn't been signed, it doesn't have a seal. And it was seized in Sarajevo, which we do not believe that is a secure source.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. -- Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next document, which appears is the P86. It's the Official Gazette of the municipality of Banja Luka, the date being the 16th of October, 1991. The next document, which is P87, is an article from a magazine or a publication called Vrana, dated the 21st of October, 1991. Your Honour, if you go to the second page, it's an article about the meeting that was held on the 15th of October and the assembly meeting. Your Honour, in the middle of page 2, there is part of the text of Mr. Karadzic, which in opening to Your Honours I played the clip of Mr. Karadzic's speech. The third paragraph was that part, second page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I must again lodge an objection that Ms. Korner is drawing your attention to a particular portion of a document and suggesting to you that that is the import of the document and its relevance, and I think that's argument, and I object that it's argument and it's improper to be making argument at this stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The objection is not being sustained, Mr. Ackerman, because to the Chamber it is obvious that this is not an argument. It's an explanation that this part, which is in quotes, in inverted commas, is actually the part which was shown in the video clip that Ms. Korner referred to. There is absolutely no comment about the content or anything to indicate to the Tribunal that the rest of the document is not important or is not being referred to by the Prosecution, so your objection is not being sustained.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, if it assists Mr. Ackerman, he's made his objection to the whole process very clear, and for the purposes of appeal, I have no doubt the appeal will note that he objects to all of this. Your Honour, the next document is P88, which is a request to the security services centre to hold a rally. It was dated the -- can't read the date apparently. No. It's been gone through. But apparently it was received, at the bottom, on the 22nd of October, and states that the people listed will be speaking at this rally. Your Honour, P22 or 89, Your Honour, was dealt with by, again, Dr. Donia when he gave his evidence, and is a telex. Then the next document, P90, is an official statement of the Muslim -- as it's described, the Muslim Bosniak organisation in Kljuc, and it relates to what is said about an instructions signed by Mr. Brdjanin, vice-president of the autonomous region. Your Honour, that document will appear again, in fact, in the Kljuc bundle when we get to it. The next document, P23 or P91, is an agenda for the Assembly of the Autonomous Region on the 6th of November, 1991. The following document, which is P92, is a decision of the Assembly of the Serbian People on the 21st of November, 1991. Your Honour, it is -- it deals with -- I was going to say regionalisation, but it talks about the Serb Autonomous Regions of Krajina, Slavonia, Baranja and Western Srem. It's signed -- not sure it is signed but it bears a seal and the name Krajisnik. Your Honour, then the next document, which is P93 -- for some reason I've crossed that out and written 448, but I don't recall why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: The record indicates that Ms. Korner said that this document, P91, bears a seal.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm looking and I can't find it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 92, not 91. The last document we dealt with was 92. And ours at least does bear a seal, obviously on the B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It's my mistake, Your Honour. I was looking at the wrong document.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Not a signature. I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] There is no signature and it was obtained from the Ministry of the Interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But you will notice, Ms. Korner, that although on the face of the last page of the B/C/S text, there is a stamp, and to me no apparent signature, in the English text, beneath the name Momcilo Krajisnik, there is "signed".

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I agree, Your Honour, it may be that it's lost on the copying but at the moment, on the face of it, it doesn't appear to have any kind of a signatures, if you look at the copy of the B/C/S version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mine doesn't. There is a beginning of a sign or something, but Madam Fauveau, yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the moment, we object to this document, particularly because it comes from the Ministry of Interior of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I thank you. You may go ahead, Ms. Korner. Anyway, you will undoubtedly check that, and if the original document that you have bears a signature, you will perhaps let us -- bring it forward so that we can see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the next document, which is P93 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Is self-explanatory.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Is the article in Oslobodenje of the 12th, of the 11th, 1991, that I referred to yesterday. In the second edition, sorry -- the next document is P94, which is further Official Gazette of the municipality of Banja Luka dated the 28th of November, 1991, and deals with -- the first part deals with the founding of Banja Luka Television Public Enterprises. It then goes on to deal with other matters further on. Your Honour, then the next document, P95, is the minutes of the tenth session of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, and that was the 14th of December, 1991. And the following document, P96, is the conclusions. The next document, Your Honour, is the still-to-be-resolved instructions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The Variant A and Variant B.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The Variant A/B and version number 100. Your Honour, then the next document is a report on paramilitary units, their activity and other current security-related events, dated the 29th of December of 1991. If one looks just for a moment at the original, because it's not so clear what's happening, the top is -- as one can see, it's headed "Kesic" and then somebody has written a note complaining, and then underneath a further note.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: P98, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I hope I've got the right number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Otherwise it's not terribly clear what the English typing means, but if you look at the original, one can see what's happened. Your Honour, the next document, P99 is the Statute of the United Serbian Democratic Parties in Serbia, Your Honour, the SDS. Your Honour, then P100 --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Excuse me just a moment. This probably has to do with my own confusion, Your Honour, but Ms. Korner represented this to be a statute of the SDS, and the text indicates that it's an organisation called the SSDS. I'm not sure this is the same organisation as the SDS we have been referring to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Korner, I confirm, she did say "of the SDS."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, the Serbian Democratic Parties. I think if one looks at --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Actually, the acronym is in the second page, penultimate paragraph of Article 1, it says letters "SSDS" in the middle part, so it is SSDS and not SDS.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I think that means "united" and stands for the word, however, but Your Honour, I take the correction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Go ahead. Exhibit -- sorry, Mr. Ackerman, I didn't recognise you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm told by my colleague who understands the language that this is not an SDS document, that it's a different organisation. So at some point, this will have to be cleared up, I take it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, I'm sure you've taken note of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is why it's proving to be an useful exercise. Your Honour, the next document which is P100, is again an agenda of the ARK Assembly dated the 6th of January, 1992. It appears to be stamped and signed. Your Honour, the next document, P101 or P31, was looked at by Dr. Donia, and is the eleventh session minutes. Then the document at P102 is conclusions of the Assembly of the Republic of the Serbian people. Well, again, it could -- it may or may not bear a signature. The stamp is pretty illegible. It comes from Bihac, this particular document, and relates to the referendum that was about to be held. Then, Your Honour, the next document.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, we object to it because the signature is not clear and because it comes from the AID in Bihac.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then, Your Honour, the next document is a monthly report of the security services in Banja Luka to the Ministry of the Interior of the Socialist Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. It's signed -- let's just check that. Well, there is a stamp and apparently a signature of Stojan Zupljanin and that actually was taken from Prijedor Police Station. Your Honour, the next document, P104, is a leaflet, apparently -- and I think it was dealt with yesterday by the witness, or the day before, or the day before that. And I think there was an objection raised then because it was just a leaflet without any accompanying --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next, P105.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Ms. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We object to this document because it comes from Bihac and it is obviously not signed. It cannot be signed. But moreover, I do not believe that this is the document that the witness was referring to that Ms. Korner just mentioned because the document that the witness was referring to was referring to the referendum linked to the Vance-Owen Plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: She may be right. Probably she is. Madam Fauveau is right, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. I don't -- I don't think so. I think it is the same document, although he had it himself. But I'll double-check that. I think it was the same document. But he produced his own version, and in fact I think I asked for it to be exhibited, forgetting that we had it in here because it comes from a different source. But I'll check that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In any case, this is being objected to by --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I understand that, Your Honour. I understand that it's being objected to.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Perhaps it is the same document, but the witness clearly said that the document that he was talking about was in relation to the referendum on the Vance-Owen Plan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next 105.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, 105 is a letter to the Minister of the Interior, signed by Mr. Kesic apparently, seeking certificates for firearms, pistols. Your Honour, then the next document, which is P106, also P36, because it was looked at by Dr. Donia, and it's conclusions again. P107 is an article in Glas headed "Brdjanin directing again," dated the 11th of February, 1992, and is the resignation -- the subject is "Celinac. Resignation of Dr. Milorad Kuzmanovic, president of the Serbian Democratic Party's municipal board. Under the microscope." And there is quite a long article about that. The next document are the -- which is P108 is the minutes of a meeting held in Banja Luka and appears to be - I can't say any more than that - minutes of a meeting concerning the Ministry of the Interior.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We object to this document because we don't know exactly what was the body that they had a meeting; it doesn't have a seal; and it was obtained from Sarajevo, the Security Services Centre in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, all I can say is by reading the text, it appears to be in connection with police work in various areas. But that's all one can say.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly. But we don't know who these people are who met in order to discuss police work.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, that's not in fact quite right, because we've heard evidence about Stojan Zupljanin and Mr. Tutus, both of whom are mentioned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next document, Ms. Korner. Otherwise you will see Mr. Ackerman standing up.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then Your Honour, the next -- the next document is a publication called "Derventski List." It's dated the 13th of February, 1992. And it's headed "Bridge to the Krajinas." And it is in respect of the meetings of the -- a meeting of the SDS. Your Honour, then the next --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: May I ask, is Derventa a municipality or a town or a --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's a municipality, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then, Your Honour, the next document is another article in Glas, which is P110, and is a statement by the National Defence Council in Celinac. It appears to relate to the article we looked at earlier --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, "Brdjanin director again."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then, Your Honour, the next document is municipal -- it's meetings effectively -- abridged minutes of the 15th session of the municipal assembly in February of 1992. And it's -- in fact, it's quite a long document.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Excuse me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We object to this document because it is not a complete transcript, complete minutes, and we don't know whether what was said at the meeting are exactly as they appear in the minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm sure Ms. Korner will take note of that, as the Chamber is.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, moving along at a bit more speed, the next document, which is document -- I've just lost my --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes, 112. Thank you. Your Honour, we've already looked at.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. That was used in the -- during the --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The previous witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, 113 is an agenda for the 21st of February for a meeting to be held in the cultural centre.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Mm-hm.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The next document is P114 or P37, which is instructions concerning the plebiscite, as it's put, of the Muslim and Croat people. Then the next document, P115, an instruction to the municipal boards of the SDS, signed by Rajko Dukic. The next document, P116, is a document which is a decision that Mr. Vukic is to become the member in charge coordinator for the Autonomous Region of Krajina, signed by Mr. Dukic. Or again, it may have a signature, but it doesn't appear there's a stamp on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I appreciate --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Madam Fauveau.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Can we take it, Madam Fauveau, that -- I mean, that anything that comes from Sarajevo or whatever is objected to?

utterances.speaker: MS. FAUVEAU-IVANOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, yes, exactly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Then, Your Honour, the next --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: 117 is another article from Oslobodenje, 27th of February, 1992, which is apparently a press conference at which -- or interviews with which Brdjanin and Krajisnik were speaking. The next document is again an agenda or extract from the 14th session of ARK held on the 29th of February, 1992, which is P -- either 118 or 35, because Dr. Donia dealt with that. Then an article in Glas reporting on the session in the Krajina Assembly. It's dated the 2nd of March, and it's called "Sharing Sovereignty." And there are a number of quotes from what was said. The next one, P120 or 38, agenda for the 15th session on the 14th of March -- 4th of March. I'm so sorry, followed by a document that we've already looked at, the Radio Banja Luka, on the 6th of March, 1992. That's P121. P122, Your Honour, that is a publication called Slobodna Bosna. It's dated the 12th of March, headed "Serbs prepare for war." And in fact, it reproduces the instructions for the organisation activities of the organs of the Serbian people, the Variant A and B document, which one can see in the next few pages.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Ms. Korner, unless the English version has been taken out by my secretary and put in some other folder -- in other words, unless this document was put to a previous witness, I don't have the English text.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. Your Honour, it -- I understand we were made aware that certain documents were missing and we provided copies of -- I think what happened is some of the translations came in late. We've given to the Registry copies of all the translations and asked them to insert them in Your Honours' bundle. So it may be that before we start recopying, the Registry and Your Honours' legal officers could check, because they may be sitting around the place and just haven't been put in.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. I pointed it out, because I don't recall this document being put to any witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It hasn't been put to anybody yet. And we haven't got as far as dealing with Variant A and B, because the objection was drawn at that stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: But it wasn't to Mr. Donia either.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: To?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: To Dr. Donia either.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. I think he referred to it, but I don't think that he actually -- I think that's right. We didn't have the English translation at that stage.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead, Ms. Korner, please, 123.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. Then, Your Honour, the next document, which is P123, is a review -- it's entitled "A review of security information," addressed to the Minister of the Interior, signed by Mr. Kesic, and there is a signature on the letter. P124 would appear to be the document enclosed with the letter that we just looked at. Then the next document, P125, to all municipal boards of the Serbian Democratic Party, dated the 13th of March, in accordance with the stance adopted, required to assess the possibility of establishing a Serbian municipality in your area of activities, stamped and signed by Mr. Dukic. And that comes from the municipal assembly building in Prijedor and was actually seized by Mr. Inayat. So we could have -- Then there's an article in Glas dated the 14th of March. And I think we looked at that -- maybe not. But it's really -- it's Dr. Vukic sounding off again. Then P127 we've looked at with the last witness. P128, an article in Glas reporting on the first extraordinary convention of the Banja Luka Serbian Democratic Party. And then the next document, which is an evaluation of the security situation by the CSB, 25th of March. And it's not apparently signed. It comes from the CSB building. Then the next document, P130, is a notice or it's -- it appears to be a document from the Serbian Democratic Party of Bosnia and Herzegovina, dated the 23rd of March, addressed to all presidents of municipalities. The document bears apparently a seal and a signature, and appears to come from Dr. Karadzic. P131 is the evaluation of the security situation in the Banja Luka sector. P132 is apparently a notice that -- of the referendum. I think it must be -- almost certainly is in the wrong place, because if it's talking about the referendum taking place at the end of "this" month, I think it must -- well, we'll leave it, but I'm not sure it's in the right position. Then the next document is P133, again the security situation in Banja Luka in March. We've looked at the next document, which is P134. It's the announcement of the demands made by the SOS group. P135, we've also looked at, because it's -- it was put, I think, by Madam Fauveau, about people who wanted to change their name, to one of the earlier witnesses. Then the next document, P136, again is a Security Services Centre report, this time dated the 3rd of April, no sign or signature but taken from the CSB building. Glas, the next document, P137, again we looked at that with the last witness because it's a report of the SOS. P138, this is an unknown publication, in the sense that it appears to have been cut out and arrived from -- it says "open source." I think we ought to be able to do a bit more than that. In any event, it's an article headed "Izetbegovic Declared War" and refers to a press conference given by the SDS regional board in Banja Luka and the vice-president of the Autonomous Region speaks, and again it's in relation to the SOS. Then the next document, P139, is again a -- something that we looked at together with the last witness. P140 is an example of the loyalty oath that had to be taken by members of the CSB. The next document, P141, again, we looked at with the last witness, and I believe P142, yeah, and P143. P144 is a report from the Banja Luka -- or to the Banja Luka -- I'm sorry, from the Banja Luka SJB, which is one down from the CJB, about events that had gone on. And finally, we have a report which comes from the CSB, Your Honour, so it's a report that was found there, which talks about the deterioration in the Banja Luka region and Kotor Varos, Jajce, Sanski Most and Prijedor. And Your Honour, virtually it's bang on midday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Perfect. If Mr. Ackerman hadn't raised more objections, we would have finished a little bit earlier. Our agenda for next week is --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Holiday, I hope.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For after -- I take it you will liaise with the Defence just prior to our resumption.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we are continuing with the order as it was, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay. Yes, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like to request that we set aside maybe the first hour or hour and a half of our next sitting, because I would like to go through the defendant Brdjanin exhibits with you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The same way.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: And make suggestions and explanations with regard to them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No argument, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: No argument.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He wants to do exactly the same thing you did.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I know, Your Honour, but it's not the Defence case. Your Honour, he's perfectly entitled to do that when and if he mounts his Defence case, to take Your Honours through --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think she's right, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: The order of evidence, according to the rules --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're definitely right. You cannot introduce now and intrude now and interrupt her case to present yours. We will come to you and you will be treated exactly the same, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Anything else before we rise? So I -- we will resume on the 3rd of April, according to our agreed schedule, at 9.00 in the morning. I think the sitting is on the morning in that day, no?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, we have had no schedule yet, official schedule, as to when we are sitting.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's a pity, because I know that it is available. I know that the first week we are sitting in the morning, and as from the second week, right through the end of the month, we are sitting in the afternoon. That much I know for sure. That's about it. I do have the schedule right through July, actually, but --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour has the advantage over all of us, I feel.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Ms. Korner raises a good point. There seems to be some secrecy about the schedules here. We don't get them, I don't know why.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I will give instructions to my secretary to see that you are furnished with what we were furnished. More or less the situation as suggested to me is that in April, we are sitting mostly in the afternoon, except for the first couple of days in the first week. May, if I remember well, with the exception of a couple of days, we are sitting in the morning. June, I think it's the entire month in the afternoon. July, I think it's the entire month in the afternoon, with the exception of a week or something like that. That's -- but that's negotiable because it depends also on Stakic starting when it's starting, and also we had to see that the sharing of the courtrooms is -- anyway, in other words, it's not exactly 100 per cent definite schedule, but it is available for sure, and I have asked my secretary also to pinpoint the agreed breaks that we will be having between now and the end of July.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Yes. We very kindly received the notification from the Senior Legal Officer as to the breaks. It was simply a question whether we were sitting morning and afternoon or -- I suppose there is some rhyme or reason to doing mornings one week and afternoons the other.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The suggestion was that, but there is a problem with one of the trials that is always being heard in the morning, as you know, and that occupies one courtroom, practically it's in the morning and part of the afternoon. That leaves us with two courtrooms, and with four other ongoing trials, that is manageable. With six ongoing trials, the moment Stakic starts next month, there may be a little bit of a -- not exactly a problem, but one has to sort out --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, of course, A, I don't know whether Your Honour is aware - probably not - we have sent in an application to delay the start of Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: We've put that in for the reason that, interestingly enough, had we stuck to the original chronology, the two of them would have coincided. Now they won't. But -- which is not objected to by the Defence. But it does of course -- it's all very well saying we can run six trials, but that means unless the trial in court number -- the trial in Court number I is only going to sit mornings, there is no possibility of, it seems to me, running six trials.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The indication that I have, Ms. Korner, is that according to the schedule that I have in my possession - I don't have it with me because I didn't know we were going to discuss this in so much detail - but the indication that I have is that Courtroom number I will be used for one particular trial, and I suppose it's the same schedule that we have now. In other words, from 9.30 until 1.00 and then -- that's the impression that I have. How we are going to fit in the other five trials, I don't know, but each trial has already a break planned periodically, and I know that we will be alternating some chambers in the morning, some chambers in the afternoon. There are weeks when two trials will be alternating, as you said, two weeks in the morning, two weeks in the afternoon. It's a little bit complicated. I was more interested in this trial than in others, and in actual fact, I will be trying to see if we could actually shift some of the sittings to the morning rather than keep going in the afternoon for two solid months, even though these are months when you finish at 7.00 in the evening it's still beautiful here in The Hague, and you have ample time for what you need to do.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I don't think Your Honour has spent a summer in The Hague yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I haven't.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Saying it's beautiful in The Hague in the evenings, well, occasionally.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I haven't. I haven't. I do mean to spend the whole of August in my country where it's beautiful and hot. Anyway, we will meet again on the 3rd of April, and those of you who celebrate Easter between now and then, Happy Easter, and we will meet to resume or work as agreed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: 12.13 p.m., to be reconvened on Wednesday, the 3rd day of April, 2002, at 9.00 a.m. 25
